description: We are a creative, ambitious team that believes great ideas come from collaboration, fresh thinking, and teamwork. For “Abandoned but not Forgotten,” we want to bring NASA’s forgotten space explorers back into the spotlight through an engaging interactive experience. We are passionate, open to challenges, and determined to create something meaningful. We welcome developers, designers, researchers, storytellers, and space enthusiasts. Let's create something awesome together! 🚀
summary: "Voices of the Dust" is an interactive educational web museum developed for the "Abandoned, but Not Forgotten" challenge. Across the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space, historic spacecraft—such as the Apollo 11 lunar module, Opportunity rover, Ingenuity helicopter, and Pioneer 10—rest silently after completing their missions. This educational platform is designed not only for school-age students and university learners, but for anyone passionate about space exploration. To build this platform, we utilized comprehensive NASA open data and collaborated with AI tools (Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT). AI assisted us with coding, translating texts, and gathering more detailed, in-depth information about the missions to create a truly user-friendly and interactive website. Personally, I thoroughly enjoyed working on this challenge because of my own passion for space. The most amazing part was working with real historical tasks and spacecraft that actually operated in space—it was a truly impressive and thrilling experience!
details:
What it does & How it works "Voices of the Dust" is a 4-page interactive web applicationthat transforms discarded space hardware into engaging storytellers that the world will never forget:
Home Hub: Introduces the truly captivating scale of humanity's space heritage across the Moon, Mars, Asteroid Eros, and Deep Space.
Missions & Interactive Map (Planetary Explorer): Helps users discover in-depth information about each expedition and features clickable landing sites with real planetary coordinates, mission timelines, status badges, and telemetry logs for iconic spacecraft including Apollo 11, Apollo 12, Apollo 15, Surveyor 3, Mars Pathfinder/Sojourner, Viking 1, Opportunity, InSight, Ingenuity, NEAR Shoemaker, Dawn, Kepler, and Pioneer 10.
First-Person Rover Comics: Engaging, illustrated multi-panel comic stories told from the perspective of the machines themselves (such as Opportunity's final dust storm and Apollo 11's Eagle lander in the Sea of Tranquility) that readers will love exploring. Additionally, the website provides external resources and reference links that students can use for deeper research and future projects.
Interactive Quiz: A gamified quiz that reinforces learning and tests students on real historical mission facts.
